previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and multiple comorbidities was admitted with a four-day history of cough and pleuritic chest pain, along with new bilateral leg pain and hematuria. He had undergone dialysis earlier on the day of admission but remained symptomatic. Initial labs revealed severe hyperkalemia (K 8.3), which was treated and resolved. Chest imaging showed chronic interstitial changes without pneumonia or acute findings. He was diagnosed with bronchitis and treated with a five-day course of azithromycin. His respiratory symptoms improved, and he tolerated another dialysis session during the stay. Trace hematuria persisted without signs of infection. He remained stable, was discharged home on his baseline medications plus a short course of antibiotics, and advised to resume outpatient dialysis and follow up with his nephrologist.
